openFinding_notThisLanesToFix.statement: The eight downstream rails are blocked on S1's (parcel-setback-cells.mjs) and, by the same class, S2's (parcel-envelope-cells.mjs) writers having no branch for a not-applicable zoningDistrict -- both writers' documented gate is 'zoningDistrict has reached value or refused.' A legitimately not-applicable zoningDistrict (unzoned land in a declared-complete city) will never become value or refused, and parcel-r5-zoning's UPDATE is permanently gated to cells currently kind='unaccounted', so it will never revisit these cells either. These 3,376 parcels' setback/envelope cells are PERMANENTLY unaccounted under current logic, with zero path to resolution short of teaching S1/S2 to recognize a not-applicable zoningDistrict and propagate not-applicable onto their own rails.
openFinding_notThisLanesToFix.whyNotFixedHere: Dispatch explicitly: 'Fixing S1's deferral rule' is out of scope; 'do not fix S1's writer from here.' Reported for a successor or the operator to route.
openFinding_notThisLanesToFix.suggestedNextPlanRow: A new P-row against parcel-setback-cells.mjs / parcel-envelope-cells.mjs: when a residual parcel's zoningDistrict is kind='not-applicable', write kind='not-applicable' (with a pointer back to the zoningDistrict cell's own completenessDeclaration as the decision-record basis) on the dependent rail instead of leaving it unaccounted. Would resolve all 3,376 x 8 = 26,608 dependent cells in one pass, no further zoningDistrict work needed.

When a dispatch names a rail's 'unaccounted' residual sourced from a DOWNSTREAM writer's deferral count (S1/S4's setback/verdict-side numbers), verify the UPSTREAM rail's own literal cell_state kind directly before assuming the population is actually sitting 'unaccounted' there -- a downstream writer's own deferral condition ('not yet value or refused') can be satisfied by a state (not-applicable) that is neither 'value/refused' nor 'unaccounted', and conflating the two changes which bucket the whole residual belongs to.

parcel_record_cell is ~64M rows (65 rails x the full multi-county universe); a query filtering only on cell_state->>'kind' without a leading rail_key or place_key-prefix predicate that the query planner can use as its FIRST bitmap scan will time out even at 100s on the small autoscaling replica under concurrent fleet load. Lead with rail_key (has a plain btree index) or use the existing partial index on kind='unaccounted', never both as an unweighted AND across the full table.

See openFinding_notThisLanesToFix -- a successor plan row against parcel-setback-cells.mjs/parcel-envelope-cells.mjs should teach both writers to propagate a not-applicable zoningDistrict onto their own rails instead of deferring forever.
